A.explanation: This uses the wasted power $0.40 \times 800 = 320 \text{ W}$ instead of the useful output power, giving $320/12 \approx 27 \text{ N}$.

B.explanation: Useful power is $0.60 \times 800 = 480 \text{ W}$, so $F = P/v = 480/12 = 40 \text{ N}$, which balances the resistive force at constant velocity.

C.explanation: This ignores the 60% efficiency and uses the full input power, giving $800/12 \approx 67 \text{ N}$.

D.explanation: This divides by efficiency, $800/0.60 \approx 1333 \text{ W}$, giving $1333/12 \approx 110 \text{ N}$, which is larger than the input power allows.

hints: Notice the car moves at constant velocity of $12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so the forward driving force must equal the total horizontal resistive force.
Connect the 60% efficiency to useful power: only $0.60$ of the $800 \text{ W}$ input power drives the car, and mechanical power follows $P = Fv$.
First calculate useful power in $\text{W}$, then rearrange to $F = P/v$ and divide by $12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to get force in $\text{N}$.
walkthrough: Constant velocity in a straight horizontal line means resultant horizontal force is zero, so driving force $F$ equals total resistive force.
The engine efficiency is $\text{efficiency} = P_{useful}/P_{input}$, so the power that produces motion is less than $800 \text{ W}$.
Calculate useful output power: $P_{useful} = 0.60 \times 800 \text{ W} = 480 \text{ W}$.
Use $P = Fv$ for motion at speed $v = 12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and rearrange to $F = P_{useful}/v$.
Substitute values with units: $F = 480 \text{ W} / 12 \text{ m s}^{-1} = 40 \text{ N}$.
This driving force equals the resistive force, so the resistive force is $40 \text{ N}$. This is option B.
